title: Runtime LTS Backport Queue Tracker (runtime-1.20-lts)
sheet_purpose: Working queue of candidate backports into runtime-1.20-lts patch releases. Used by Release Eng + Runtime owners to track risk tier, required approvals, cherry-pick conflicts, test evidence, and target patch version. Not customer-facing; source of truth for release checklist and audit evidence capture.

notes_and_conventions: Risk tiers: P0-Critical (security/data integrity/release correctness), P1-High (correctness or major perf regression fix), P2-Low (tooling/docs/process; low behavior risk), P3-Medium (generally excluded from LTS unless explicitly approved as regression fix). Status glossary: CANDIDATE (not triaged), IN REVIEW (awaiting approvals/tests), CHERRY-PICK CONFLICT (needs manual minimal-diff implementation), QUEUED (approved; waiting for target patch branch window), MERGED -> LTS BRANCH (in runtime-1.20-lts), RELEASED (shipped in patch), DROPPED (explicitly excluded; keep rationale).
next_triage_meeting: Weekly backport triage: Tuesdays 10:00–10:30 PT (Connor, Omar, Sofia, Hiro, Sean). Add new candidates with: PR link, why/trigger, risk tier proposal, and required test plan. Anything P0/P1 needs explicit SRE sign-off before inclusion.
open_questions: For scheduler fixes with refactor divergence: do we allow “re-implement minimal patch” on LTS branch without cherry-pick hash parity, if provenance includes manual diff review notes?
For metrics cardinality fixes: can we treat dashboard-impact changes as P1 if they reduce incident risk, even though they break some dashboards?
Embargo workflow: what’s the minimum public release note wording allowed for private customers without CVE assignment?
